_comment: Batch 08 (Sets 14-15). Distractor-only rewrites to remove the longest-answer cue. Correct options, stems, and rationales are unchanged; each distractor keeps its original meaning and stays wrong for the same reason. PN-S15-08 (injection angles) is in skipped.json as numeric.

RN-S14-01.B: A client with schizophrenia who reports hearing voices commenting on the weather, which staff note is the client's usual pattern
RN-S14-01.C: A client with anorexia nervosa who is refusing to finish breakfast and is asking to skip the morning weigh-in
RN-S14-01.D: A client with bipolar disorder who is pacing in the hallway and talking rapidly but is redirectable by staff

RN-S14-06.A: Aged cheddar cheese and sliced dry salami on wheat crackers
RN-S14-06.C: Pepperoni pizza with a glass of draft beer on tap
RN-S14-06.D: Vegetable stir-fry with soy sauce and fermented tofu

RN-S14-08.A: Administer the next scheduled dose of haloperidol on time as prescribed
RN-S14-08.C: Encourage ambulation to help relieve the muscle rigidity
RN-S14-08.D: Apply warm blankets to help relax the rigid muscles

RN-S14-09.A: Tell the client this is most likely a common cold, and encourage rest and plenty of fluids at home
RN-S14-09.C: Give an extra dose of clozapine now and recheck the temperature in 4 hours
RN-S14-09.D: Encourage warm salt-water gargles only and recheck the temperature at bedtime

RN-S14-10.B: An additional dose of haloperidol IM now

RN-S14-11.A: "Yes, I can hear them too. Let's sit down together and figure out what they want from you."
RN-S14-11.C: "There are no voices here. Stop imagining things and try to focus on reality."
RN-S14-11.D: "Let's not talk about the voices right now. Tell me about your family instead."

RN-S14-12.A: Insist that the client sit at the table and finish full meals with the group
RN-S14-12.C: Serve meals in the busy dining room to encourage socializing with peers
RN-S14-12.D: Withhold snacks until the client sits down and finishes a full meal

RN-S14-16.A: Obtain a restraint prescription that is renewed each day without reassessing the client, so the restraints can stay on for as long as needed for safety
RN-S14-16.C: Keep the client restrained until the next day to ensure safety, even if the client becomes calm and cooperative this evening
RN-S14-16.D: Tie the restraints to the side rails with a quick-release knot so they can be loosened easily if the client needs care

RN-S14-17.A: Tell the client firmly that there's nothing on the unit to be afraid of right now
RN-S14-17.C: Touch the client firmly on the shoulder without warning to get attention
RN-S14-17.D: Ask the client to describe the traumatic event in detail right now

RN-S14-18.A: Naloxone causes permanent sedation that develops after the client wakes up
RN-S14-18.C: Naloxone causes hypoglycemia that typically develops within the first hour
RN-S14-18.D: Close monitoring is no longer needed once the client wakes up and is talking normally

RN-S14-19.A: "You'll have permanent memory loss after these treatments, so you won't remember much about your own past."
RN-S14-19.C: "You'll be fully awake during the treatment, and you will feel the seizure as it happens."
RN-S14-19.D: "There are no side effects at all from ECT, so there's nothing to worry about afterward."

RN-S15-01.B: A scheduled oral stool softener for a client with no bowel movement in 2 days
RN-S15-01.C: PRN acetaminophen for a headache rated 3/10 that started an hour ago
RN-S15-01.D: A daily oral multivitamin that is scheduled for 0900 with breakfast

RN-S15-09.A: Administer the next dose of lisinopril as scheduled with a glass of water
RN-S15-09.C: Apply ice packs to the lips and tongue and recheck the swelling in 30 minutes
RN-S15-09.D: Reassure the client that this is a mild, expected side effect of lisinopril

RN-S15-11.A: Checking the room number and bed number against the medication administration record
RN-S15-11.B: Asking "Are you Mr. Jones?" and waiting for the client to answer yes before giving any of the medications
RN-S15-11.D: Asking the client's roommate to confirm the client's full name before giving the medications

RN-S15-13.A: Save it in a labeled syringe in the locked medication room for the client's next dose
RN-S15-13.C: Discard it in the sharps container without a witness and document the waste alone
RN-S15-13.D: Give the rest to the client later in the shift if the pain comes back again

RN-S15-15.A: Immediately after the vancomycin infusion is finished
RN-S15-15.C: Two hours after the dose has finished infusing
RN-S15-15.D: At any convenient time of day during the shift

RN-S15-16.A: Start with higher doses to overcome the slower absorption that occurs with aging
RN-S15-16.C: Older adults need fewer monitoring visits once a medication is started
RN-S15-16.D: Drug interactions are less common in older adults than in younger adults

RN-S15-18.A: No change in INR monitoring is needed while on the antibiotic
RN-S15-18.C: Doubling the warfarin dose for as long as the client takes the antibiotic
RN-S15-18.D: Stopping warfarin permanently once the antibiotic is started

RN-S15-19.A: "Yes, pressing the button for her while she sleeps will keep her pain under control, so she won't wake up hurting in the middle of the night tonight."
RN-S15-19.C: "You can press it for her, but only once every hour, so she gets a steady amount of pain medicine while she sleeps."
RN-S15-19.D: "Only press it for her if she is groaning or looks uncomfortable in her sleep, so she doesn't wake up in pain."

PN-S14-01.B: Determining a client's level of suicide risk at the start of the shift
PN-S14-01.C: Reinforcing medication teaching with a client being discharged home
PN-S14-01.D: Deciding when a client can come off one-to-one suicide precautions

PN-S14-02.A: "That's not true at all. You're a great person."
PN-S14-02.C: "Everybody feels that way sometimes, so don't worry."
PN-S14-02.D: "You shouldn't say things like that about yourself."

PN-S14-04.A: Leave the client alone in a quiet room for a few minutes to calm down
PN-S14-04.C: Ask the client to explain in detail what triggered the attack
PN-S14-04.D: Encourage the client to join a group activity to take their mind off it

PN-S14-07.A: "Drinking a small glass of wine with it in the evening is fine, as long as you eat first."
PN-S14-07.C: "You can double the dose on days when you feel more anxious than usual, then go back."
PN-S14-07.D: "It is safe to take together with your opioid pain medicine after your knee surgery."

PN-S14-08.A: "Stop taking the medication until your mouth feels better."
PN-S14-08.C: "Drink sugary soda throughout the day to keep your mouth moist."
PN-S14-08.D: "Use an alcohol-based mouthwash several times a day."

PN-S14-09.D: Pupil size and reactivity to light

PN-S14-10.A: Gradual memory loss that has slowly and steadily worsened over several years
PN-S14-10.C: A stable level of consciousness and attention throughout the day
PN-S14-10.D: An irreversible decline in thinking that progresses over time

PN-S14-11.A: Enjoying weekly visits with family members and looking forward to the next visit each Sunday
PN-S14-11.C: Mild forgetfulness about the names of new staff members and neighbors in the building
PN-S14-11.D: Waking up once each night to void and then falling back asleep easily afterward

PN-S14-12.A: "I can keep using my regular mouthwash that contains alcohol after I brush my teeth."
PN-S14-12.C: "I can still have one beer a day with dinner without having any problems."
PN-S14-12.D: "This medication will reduce my cravings for alcohol so I won't want to drink."

PN-S14-13.A: Allow the client to eat meals alone in their room to reduce stress at mealtimes
PN-S14-13.C: Weigh the client in street clothes at varying times of the day
PN-S14-13.D: Discuss food choices and calorie counts with the client at length

PN-S14-14.A: Assign different staff members to the child each shift so that the child experiences more variety
PN-S14-14.C: Place the child in the busy playroom with other children to encourage play
PN-S14-14.D: Frequently rearrange the child's room and toys to keep the child interested

PN-S14-16.A: Explore the client's childhood experiences and early family relationships
PN-S14-16.C: Schedule long-term psychotherapy to begin in the next few weeks
PN-S14-16.D: Discuss the home insurance paperwork and claims process in detail

PN-S14-17.A: Ask the client about abuse in front of the partner to get both sides
PN-S14-17.C: Ignore the bruises, since the client has not mentioned them
PN-S14-17.D: Confront the partner about the bruises on the client's arms

PN-S14-18.B: Check the client and the restraints once per shift, and document the findings in the client's record at the end of the shift
PN-S14-18.C: Secure the restraints to the side rails of the bed so they can be adjusted quickly when the client needs to be repositioned
PN-S14-18.D: Use a tight knot that cannot be released quickly, so the client is not able to untie the restraints and climb out of the bed during the night

PN-S14-19.A: Call security right away so that they can help staff place the client in restraints
PN-S14-19.C: Turn your back to the client to show that you are not a threat to them
PN-S14-19.D: Argue with the client about why the behavior is not acceptable on the unit

PN-S14-20.A: "Drink a cup of coffee after dinner to help you relax in the evening."
PN-S14-20.C: "Take long naps during the day to make up for the sleep you've lost."
PN-S14-20.D: "Exercise vigorously right before bed so you'll be tired enough to sleep."

PN-S14-21.A: Prevent the client from washing their hands so that they get to breakfast on time
PN-S14-21.C: Tell the client there will be consequences for being late to breakfast again
PN-S14-21.D: Point out to the client how unnecessary and silly the handwashing is

PN-S14-23.A: Pinpoint pupils, drowsiness, and slow, shallow respirations of 8/min
PN-S14-23.C: Hypothermia, bradycardia, and a low blood pressure reading
PN-S14-23.D: Sedation, slurred speech, nodding off, and constipation

PN-S15-01.A: Checking the client's name on the door sign and on the card at the head of the bed
PN-S15-01.C: Asking "Are you Mrs. Smith?" and giving the medications as soon as the client nods yes
PN-S15-01.D: Relying on recognizing the client's face from having cared for the same client on the previous day shift

PN-S15-05.A: "About 1 teaspoon, measured with the marked dosing cup or an oral syringe."
PN-S15-05.C: "About 1 tablespoon, measured with the marked dosing cup or an oral syringe."
PN-S15-05.D: "About 1 ounce, measured with the marked dosing cup or an oral syringe."

PN-S15-09.A: To speed up the absorption of the medication from the muscle tissue into the client's bloodstream
PN-S15-09.C: To reduce the total amount of medication needed to reach a therapeutic effect
PN-S15-09.D: To allow a larger volume of medication to be injected safely into the deltoid muscle

PN-S15-10.B: Divide the buttock into four equal quadrants using the gluteal fold and the iliac crest as landmarks, then inject at a 90-degree angle into the center of the lower inner quadrant of the buttock
PN-S15-10.C: Locate the acromion process, measure 3 fingerbreadths below it on the lateral upper arm, and inject at a 90-degree angle into the center of that muscle
PN-S15-10.D: Divide the thigh into thirds between the greater trochanter and the knee, and inject into the middle third of the outer (lateral) thigh muscle

PN-S15-11.A: Place the drop directly onto the center of the cornea while the client tilts the head back and looks upward
PN-S15-11.C: Touch the dropper tip gently to the lower eyelid to steady it while instilling the drop
PN-S15-11.D: Have the client squeeze the eye shut tightly for 1 minute afterward to keep the medication in

PN-S15-14.A: "Swallow it whole with a full glass of water, the same way that you would take any other tablet."
PN-S15-14.C: "Chew it thoroughly first, then swallow it with a small sip of water or juice."
PN-S15-14.D: "Place it between your cheek and your gum, and then swallow it after about 1 minute."

PN-S15-15.A: Position the client on the right side and insert the lubricated suppository about 1 inch, just inside the anal opening, without passing the sphincter
PN-S15-15.C: Insert the lubricated suppository directly into a mass of stool in the rectum so that it stays in place and dissolves
PN-S15-15.D: Have the client stand and bend forward over the bed while the lubricated suppository is inserted into the rectum

PN-S15-16.A: Crush the medication and hide it in the client's applesauce so the client takes it without knowing
PN-S15-16.C: Tell the client firmly that they must take the blood pressure medication because the provider prescribed it for them
PN-S15-16.D: Document that the medication was given, since the client usually takes it every morning without any problem

PN-S15-18.A: At the start of the next nursing shift
PN-S15-18.C: Only if the client puts on the call light

PN-S15-19.A: Sign the count now so that the off-going nurse can leave on time, and look for the missing tablet later in the shift
PN-S15-19.C: Replace the missing tablet with one from another client's supply so that the count is correct before signing
PN-S15-19.D: Ignore the discrepancy, since a single missing tablet is not significant enough to report to the charge nurse

PN-S15-20.A: Tell the client to stop taking whichever medications seem least important, to cut down on the number of pills
PN-S15-20.C: Suggest filling prescriptions at several different pharmacies so the client can get each medication at the lowest price
PN-S15-20.D: Advise the client to take all of the medications at the same time each morning to keep things simple

PN-S15-22.A: "Yes, grapefruit juice improves the medicine's effect safely, so you can keep drinking a glass every morning."
PN-S15-22.C: "You can drink it, but only at night, a few hours away from when you take your medication."
PN-S15-22.D: "It doesn't matter how much grapefruit juice you drink while you take this medication."

PN-S15-23.A: "No changes are needed, because rifampin and your birth control pills don't affect each other at all."
PN-S15-23.C: "Stop taking your birth control pills completely until you have finished the rifampin."
PN-S15-23.D: "Take your birth control pills twice a day instead of once while you're taking the rifampin."
